newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE closes higher but investors remain.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE closes higher but investors remain.

text.p: UK blue chips clawed back some of yesterday's losses to close higher on Tuesday albeit in very cautious trade ahead of decisions on near term interest rate policy both here and in the U.S.

The FTSE 100 index finished 3.1 points higher at 4,260.9 but well off the day's best levels, which saw the index set a new intraday high of 4,276.3. Gainers and losers were evenly matched whilst the broader Mid-250 index edged up 0.8 points to 4,575.7.
UK shares got off to a good start, supported by firm futures and gilts and in the absense of any nasty surprises from New York overnight.
The Dow had ended roughly at the same level as it was trading when London markets had closed on Monday.
Sentiment was helped amid hopes that both UK and U.S. interest rates will remain unchanged after this week's policy meetings on both sides of the Atlantic.
But activity remained subdued as most investors preferred not to take positions ahead of the outcome of the policy discussions and any possible surprise decision on rates.
The two-day U.S. FOMC meeting got underway today but no announcement was expected until late on Wednesday.
The Dow was trading 22 points lower as London markets closed, which prompted the FTSE to lose most of its earlier gains.
British policy makers are scheduled to meet tomorrow.
"If anybody is looking for a change in rates it will probably be here rather than in the U.S.," said one dealer. "But neither looks very likely."

"It's very quiet at the moment," one trader said. "We're waiting for the outcome of the meetings and we have some big company results coming up." Traders said the approaching results season was partly responsible for recent inactivity because of worries over sterling related downgrades.
"We are waiting to see if sterling is going to be a problem in the second half," a dealer said. "Pace Micro (Technology) surprised us all this morning."

The satellite and cable television equipment maker said in a trading update that sterling had put pressure on margins and prices. Pace Micro said it was forced to "re-evaluate our approach to local currency pricing, purchasing and manufacturing." The shares fell 24 percent to close at 170-1/2p.
"The UK market's price earnings ratio is very demanding," a trader said. "Results that are in line with expectations may not be good enough."

Elsewhere, traders said recent economic statistics in the U.S. appeared to show non-inflationary growth, allaying fears of the need for an interest rate rise. In the UK, economists expect the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke to continue to resist a rate rise so close to an election.
Optimism on the interest rate front helped bolster UK bank shares, dealers said. National Westminster Plc led the advance, rising 14p to 787-1/2 and Standard Chartered climbed 11p to 773-1/2p.
Meanwhile, sterling's bounce against the dollar and D-mark weighed on the pharmaceutical sector.
Zeneca finished 28-1/2p lower at 17.59 stg. Shares in SmithKline Beecham fell 19p to 873-1/2p and Glaxo Wellcome Plc eased 1-1/2p to 992.

Shares in British Telecom rose after news that the company had won Germany's fourth mobile 'phone licence. The stock gained 4-1/2p to 430p. Elsewhere in the sector Cable & Wireless shares put on 14-1/2p to 478-1/2p, after the company said it was in talks with German utility Veba AG about the future of their alliance.
British Aerospace was among the losers as speculation continued that BAe could lose out on a Saudi defence contract.
-- Elaine Hardcastle, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
